chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"The dowry (Sadaq) is that which the people mutually agree upon, whether it be little or much, and that is the dowry."

key_terms.الصَّدَاقُ: The dowry or bridal gift given by the husband to the wife
key_terms.قَلِيلًا كَانَ أَوْ كَثِيرًا: Whether it be little or much

ai.seo_question: What determines the validity of the dowry amount in Shia Islamic marriage law?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the flexibility of the dowry (mahr) as a contractual element determined by mutual consent (taradhi), reflecting the Shia juristic view that there is no fixed minimum or maximum limit. It highlights the practical implication that the validity of the marriage contract relies on the agreement of the parties rather than a specific monetary threshold, reinforcing the principle of ease in marital transactions. This ruling is foundational in distinguishing the mahr from other fixed financial obligations in Islamic law.
